 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. David Stearns made it clear at the GM meeting this month that the Mets would acquire a starting pitcher this offseason. 
 And at the top of that list figures to be Tarik Skubal, who met with team officials this past week as he goes after perhaps the most expensive contract for a starting pitcher in major league history.

 Jonah Tong, looking to secure a spot in the Mets' rotation, doesn't know where he'll wind up in the team's plans heading into 2027, but he's well aware of what Skubal would mean to the team. 
 "It's the biggest talk in free agency right now and, honestly, I would love for him to come here," Tong said. "He's a great pitcher, obviously. Like everybody we have on our current staff, he's just another bulldog we could have in our stable. It would be a really cool opportunity to learn from a guy as decorated as he is."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 23-year-old Tong took part Friday in the team's MetsGiving Turkey Giveaway at Queensborough Community College. 
 And he knows that even without Skubal in Queens, Tong has his work cut out for himself to open the season — whenever that happens — at Citi Field. 
 In addition to Nolan McLean, the Mets will be counting on Christian Scott and Zac Thornton, as well as Sean Manaea and Tylor Megill, who is coming back from Tommy John surgery. 
 Mets pitcher Jonah Tong handing out turkeys at Queensborough Community College. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post
 Kodai Senga could also have a chance to return to the rotation . 
 "Guys got a good glimpse of that end of the year," Tong said of the state of the rotation. "We have a lot of really strong pieces to the foundation. I'm really excited moving forward. My job is to try to compete and contribute as much as I possibly can."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Added to the equation is the uncertainty surrounding the sport as it careens towards a lockout that is set to begin when the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. 
 Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches the top of the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in Los Angeles, Sunday, Aug. 16, 2026. Carlin Stiehl for CA Post
 Tong, who's living with Scott this offseason in South Florida, said he's treating this offseason as he would any other. 
 His 2026 season ended well, when he struck out a career-high nine in his final start. 
 Overall, though, Tong struggled and spent much of the year at Triple-A Syracuse. 
 "It's all lived experience," Tong said of his season. "It was a cool way to end the year … It's just about getting back to being myself."
 Mets starting pitcher Jonah Tong throws to the Baltimore Orioles. JASON SZENES FOR NEW YORK POST
 Mets pitcher Jonah Tong speaking to the media after handing out turkeys at Queensborough Community College. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post
 The Mets are waiting to see exactly what that is . 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He was the organization's top pitching prospect heading into last year following the trade of Brandon Sproat and in a pair of stints in the majors this past year, Tong had a 3.82 ERA over seven appearances. 
 But he's consistently walked too many batters and in '26, did so both in the majors (4.1 per nine innings) and in the minors (5.0).
 To become a mainstay in the rotation, Tong will have to show more.
 "The onus is on me to do everything I possibly can this offseason to go out and compete and give myself a real good base going into spring training and see how it goes," Tong said. "Fortunately, I'm very young, so I have to learn a lot."
